Lhotse :: Climbing :: chunk_0005
An early attempt on Lhotse was made by the 1955 International Himalayan Expedition, headed by [Norman Dyhrenfurth](/wiki/Norman_Dyhrenfurth "Norman Dyhrenfurth"). It also included two Austrians (cartographers Erwin Schneider and Ernst Senn) and two Swiss (Bruno Spirig and Arthur Spöhel), and was the first expedition in the Everest area to include Americans ([Fred Beckey](/wiki/Fred_Beckey "Fred Beckey"), [George Bell](/wiki/George_Irving_Bell "George Irving Bell"), and Richard McGowan). The Nepalese liaison officer was Gaya Nanda Vaidya. They were accompanied by 200 local porters and several climbing [Sherpas](/wiki/Sherpa_people "Sherpa people"). After a brief look at the dangerous southern approaches of Lhotse Shar, they turned their attention, during September and October, to the [Western Cwm](/wiki/Western_Cwm "Western Cwm") and the northwest face of Lhotse, on which they achieved an altitude of about 8,100 metres (26,600 ft). They were beaten back by unexpectedly strong wind and low temperatures. Under Schneider's direction, they completed the first map of the Everest area (1:50,000 [photogrammetric](/wiki/Photogrammetry "Photogrammetry")). The expedition also made several short films covering local cultural topics and made a number of first ascents of smaller peaks in the [Khumbu](/wiki/Khumbu "Khumbu") region.[[7]](#cite_note-AAJ_1956-8)

The main summit of Lhotse was first climbed on 18 May 1956, by the Swiss team of [Ernst Reiss](/wiki/Ernst_Reiss "Ernst Reiss") and [Fritz Luchsinger](/wiki/Fritz_Luchsinger "Fritz Luchsinger"), members of the Swiss Mount Everest/Lhotse Expedition.[[8]](#cite_note-Everest_Lhotse_1956-9)[[9]](#cite_note-AAJ_1957-10)

On 12 May 1970, [Sepp Mayerl](/wiki/Sepp_Mayerl "Sepp Mayerl") and Rolf Walter of Austria made the first ascent of Lhotse Shar.[[10]](#cite_note-11)

On 12 May 1999 [Czech](/wiki/Czechs "Czechs") climber [Soňa Vomáčková](/w/index.php?title=So%C5%88a_Vom%C3%A1%C4%8Dkov%C3%A1&action

Christie was born into a wealthy upper-middle-class family in [Torquay](/wiki/Torquay "Torquay"), Devon, and was largely home-schooled. She was initially an unsuccessful writer with six consecutive rejections, but this changed in 1920, when *[The Mysterious Affair at Styles](/wiki/The_Mysterious_Affair_at_Styles "The Mysterious Affair at Styles")*, featuring detective Hercule Poirot, was published. Her first husband was [Archibald Christie](/wiki/Archie_Christie "Archie Christie"); they married in 1914 and had one child before divorcing in 1928. Following the breakdown of her marriage and the death of her mother in 1926, she made international headlines by going missing for 11 days. During both world wars, she served in hospital dispensaries, acquiring a thorough knowledge of the poisons that featured in many of her novels, short stories, and plays. Following her marriage to archaeologist [Max Mallowan](/wiki/Max_Mallowan "Max Mallowan") in 1930, she spent several months each year on archaeological excavations in the Middle East and used her first-hand knowledge of this profession in her fiction.

According to [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s [Index Translationum](/wiki/Index_Translationum "Index Translationum"), she remains the most-translated individual author.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Her novel *[And Then There Were None](/wiki/And_Then_There_Were_None "And Then There Were None")* is one of the [top-selling books](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_books "List of best-selling books") of all time, with about 100 million copies sold. Qinghai is located on the northeastern part of the [Tibetan Plateau](/wiki/Tibetan_Plateau "Tibetan Plateau"). By area, it is the largest province in the People's Republic of China (excluding the [autonomous regions](/wiki/Autonomous_regions_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "Autonomous regions of the People's Republic of China")).

The [Yellow River](/wiki/Yellow_River "Yellow River") originates in the southern part of the province, while the [Yangtze](/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River") and [Mekong](/wiki/Mekong "Mekong") have their sources in the southwestern part. Qinghai is separated by the [Riyue Mountain](/wiki/Riyue_Mountain "Riyue Mountain") into pastoral and agricultural zones in the west and east.[[30]](#cite_note-Cao-31)

The [Sanjiangyuan National Nature Reserve](/wiki/Sanjiangyuan_National_Nature_Reserve "Sanjiangyuan National Nature Reserve") is located in Qinghai and contains the headwaters of the [Yellow River](/wiki/Yellow_River "Yellow River"), [Yangtze River](/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River"), and [Mekong River](/wiki/Mekong_River "Mekong River"). The reserve was established to protect the headwaters of these three rivers and consists of 18 subareas, each containing three zones which are managed with differing degrees of strictness.

[Qinghai Lake](/wiki/Qinghai_Lake "Qinghai Lake") is the largest salt water lake in China, and the second largest in the world. Other large lakes are [Lake Hala](/wiki/Lake_Hala "Lake Hala") in the [Qilian mountains](/wiki/Qilian_Mountains "Qilian Mountains"), lakes [Gyaring](/wiki/Gyaring_Lake "Gyaring Lake") and [Ngoring](/wiki/Ngoring_Lake "Ngoring Lake") in the headwater region of the Yellow River, [Lake Donggi Cona](/wiki/Donggi_Cona "Donggi Cona"), and many saline and [salt lakes](/wiki/Salt_lake "Salt lake") in the western part of the province.

The Sixers slumped until acquiring [Julius Erving](/wiki/Julius_Erving "Julius Erving") before the [1977 season](/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_NBA_season "1976–77 NBA season"). They became a contender in the East, and in Erving's first season with the team, the Sixers eliminated the defending champion Boston Celtics in a tough seven-game Eastern semifinals in 1977. Boston slumped for the next two seasons while Philadelphia continued to be a strong team in the NBA, but in 1979, the Celtics drafted [Indiana State](/wiki/Indiana_State "Indiana State") forward [Larry Bird](/wiki/Larry_Bird "Larry Bird") in the hope of reviving their glory years as a franchise. Bird joined the team for the [1980 season](/wiki/1979%E2%80%9380_NBA_season "1979–80 NBA season") and his impact was immediate. The Celtics improved from a 29–53 record in the 1978–79 season to a league-best 61–21 record in 1979–1980, advancing to the Eastern Conference Finals that season to face the Sixers. The Sixers beat Boston in 5 but failed to win the title against the Lakers.

The next season, both the Celtics and the Sixers finished with the best record in the NBA at 62–20, but Boston held the tiebreaker in the ranking. In a classic 7-game Eastern Finals, the Celtics beat the 76ers in 1981 4–3, coming all the way back from a 3–1 deficit to win the next 3 games in classic finishes. The Celtics won Games 5 and 6 by 2 points each and the seventh game by 1 point, 91–90, coming back from a 7-point deficit with a few minutes left to win on a Larry Bird banker from the left side with barely a minute left. The Celtics then defeated the Houston Rockets on their way to their first title in 5 years. For the 1981–1982 season, the Celtics again had the best record in the NBA at 63–19, followed by Philadelphia at 58–24, with one of the Sixers' key victories in the regular season being a win in Boston to snap the Celtics' 18-game winning streak. As established by Columbia University's governing statutes, it is the duty of the president to exercise jurisdiction over all affairs of the university; to call special meetings of the University Senate, faculties, and administration; to report to the [Trustees of Columbia](/wiki/Trustees_of_Columbia_University_in_the_City_of_New_York "Trustees of Columbia University in the City of New York") on the state and needs of the university annually; and to administer discipline. According to the university charter and statutes, the consent of the president is necessary for any act made by a faculty or administrative board, unless their veto is overridden by two-thirds vote.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) Additionally, the president is able to grant leaves of absences, give faculty permission to use university laboratories for experiments, and confer academic and honorary degrees on behalf of the board of trustees.[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)

The president is *ex officio* a permanent member of the [Pulitzer Prize Board](/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize#Board "Pulitzer Prize"), and has annually presented the awards to its recipients since 1984.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In addition, the president is a member of the board of trustees of [Teachers College](/wiki/Teachers_College,_Columbia_University "Teachers College, Columbia University") and an *ex officio* member of the board of trustees of [Barnard College](/wiki/Barnard_College "Barnard College").[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)
